doc.title: Michael Moore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Jazz guitarist father and music-teacher mother
summary: His father was a jazz guitarist who wept over Charlie Christian solos, and his mother a music teacher; Moore grew up on jazz records.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well your father was a guitarist, and it was a musical family situation?

Yeah, it was. My father was a jazz guitarist and a very good one. And my mother was a vocal music teacher and piano major and taught piano and taught music, actually was my music teacher in elementary school when I was going to school. So yeah, I grew up listening to a lot of great jazz records, from the time I was very little. And I think I certainly got my passion for the music from my father, because he was very passionate,
playing Charlie Christian solos over and over, and tears running down his eyes, you know, things like that.
And I saw that from the time I was a kid. He was affected very emotionally by the music as I was and so that was a very important beginning.
